title: A Gaia DR3 scatter search of 47 million dwarf-band stars finds a new 9-year, 4.6-mag dimming of a K star; it and Gaia20cdd are kinematically old, and Gaia20cdd dimmed from 2010 to 2025
abstract: Prior campaign studies found that small dust grains cause the deep dips of the old K-type star Gaia20cdd. We tested the age of the host and searched for similar stars with public data that those studies did not use. Gaia20cdd is 1.05 kpc above the Galactic plane, so it needs a mid-plane vertical speed of at least 52 km/s, and its sky velocity relative to the local standard of rest is at least 81 km/s. Isothermal-disc models give a thick-disc probability of 0.56-0.93 and less than 1e-7 for an age below 1 Gyr. Its Gaia DR3 mean photometry includes dips; at the quiet level and quiet PS1/SDSS colour (BP-RP 0.99-1.05, not 1.18) it is 0.41-0.68 mag above the 100-pc dwarf locus, which a near-equal binary explains. TESS 2-min data (8 sectors, 2024) and ZTF exclude coherent spot modulation of 1 percent or more. Pan-STARRS1 shows new dips in 2010, 2011 and 2014 (up to 1.2 mag), so the dimming has continued for at least 15 years, with 12 percent of nights more than 0.3 mag deep. Only periods of 2888-2976 d put the 2014 and 2022 deep episodes on one orbit without conflict with 1618 quiet epochs; this predicts a deep event between 2030 April 30 and September 25. A blind search of Gaia DR3 for stars with G-band scatter above 8 percent in the dwarf band (4,559 candidates from 4.7e7 stars), followed by ZTF DR24, gives 12 long-dip dippers and recovers Gaia20cdd. The deepest is new: Gaia DR3 2870538750879109504, a K star 0.56 kpc below the plane, faded chromatically from about 2012 to 2020 (dg/dr = 1.59), dropped 4.6 mag in g for 17 days in 2020 September-October, and recovered in 2021; its kinematics also indicate an old host. Limitations: no spectra or radial velocities; the binary and the 8-year orbit are not proven; search completeness is low and not measured; 5 of the 12 dippers stay unclear. The 2014 and 2022 deep episodes and the predicted 2030 repeat window (if the period is 7.9-8.1 years) are shaded. The bottom panel shows the new Pan-STARRS1 dips of 2010-2014.

The new dimming event of the K star Gaia DR3 2870538750879109504 in ZTF DR24: a chromatic low state in 2018-2020, a 4.6 mag g dip in 2020 September-October (right: zoom), and a constant star from 2021 to 2025.

Left: the Gaia DR3 photometric-scatter search, from 141,832 high-scatter stars to 12 ZTF long-dip dippers and 2 deep field dippers. Right: height above the plane and tangential velocity of the 12 dippers by vetting group.

citations.reason: We use its Gaia alert light curves and alerts index. Its main-sequence ridge puts Gaia20cdd 0.21 mag above the ridge; our 100-pc locus gives 0.93 mag with DR3 photometry and 0.41-0.68 mag at the quiet colour.

We use its ZTF DR24 light curve, dip list and TESS fits of Gaia20cdd. We support its old-host and replenished-dust picture with a quantitative kinematic test and a 15-year dip record; we revise the quiet colour (BP-RP about 1.0, not 1.18).
